extracted.intended_audience: OMB staff and federal agency administrative/policy officials (e.g., NFAC administrative staff, agency economic researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for drafting an OMB circular or agency policy on charging for employee parking, emphasizing energy conservation, transit access, exemptions, and implementation steps. Intended to inform decisions about fee levels, exemptions, and coordination with transit providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess adequacy of public transportation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'First... is the lack of adequate public transportation available not only from places such as West Virginia where many of our employees live but from a great many areas in northern Virginia and Maryland.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before imposing parking charges, evaluate local public transit availability and coverage; do not assume transit can be readily provided. The memo warns that OMB's suggestion to resolve this through discussions with transit companies provides no assurance of favorable resolution, so lack of service is a substantive constraint on charging employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid financially penalizing employees without transit access
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The lack of adequate public transportation should not result in a financial penalty to federal employees.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should include protections (exemptions, reduced charges, or alternatives) for employees who cannot reasonably use public transportation due to geographic or scheduling constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive parking charges for those unable to carpool or use transit
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Those without access to adequate public transportation and unable to locate or form a carpool should not be made to pay an excessive parking charge in addition to the high cost of operating a vehicle.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set fee levels mindful of total commuting burdens; apply minimal rather than punitive charges where alternatives are unavailable. Consider surveys to gauge whether better transit/carpool options would change behavior before setting high fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey employee willingness and commuting options
rubrics_metrics.description: 'An intensive survey may well show that given access to reasonably scheduled public transportation or carpools, many more employees would discontinue driving alone to and from work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct surveys to determine how many employees would use mass transit or carpools if available and to inform the design of services (schedules, routes) and fee structures. Use survey results to justify service negotiations and to target incentives rather than blanket fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide exceptions or compensation for irregular-hour workers
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Another group... are those people who work irregular hours. Many people in OER would fall into this category and rarely if ever would they be able to utilize public transportation or join car pools. Therefore, it would be unfair to penalize them financially... It would almost seem more reasonable to pay them an additional sum for demands made by their job rather than charge an excessive parking fee.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and exempt or compensate employees with irregular or nonstandard schedules who cannot reasonably use transit or carpooling; consider pay differentials rather than parking charges for work-schedule burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize energy conservation as the primary goal
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Since energy conservation is the primary goal in this exercise and the utilization of car pools and mass transportation systems is being urged to accomplish this goal...',''
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the circular so that fee levels, exemptions, and incentives serve the stated objective of energy conservation. Fees should be a means to reduce single-occupancy vehicle trips, not merely a revenue source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor positive incentives and service provision over punitive fees
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Perhaps a more positive approach to the problem should be taken rather than the negative one suggested by large parking fees.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize creating or guaranteeing transit service (e.g., scheduled buses, fringe parking connections) and carpool support, rather than relying primarily on high parking fees to coerce behavior change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiate guaranteed transit service and fringe parking arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A survey should be conducted to determine those willing to routinely take a bus to and from work and then establish with the transit company a guaranteed number of passengers between particularly well-populated points (fringe parking areas) and the Headquarters building for instance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey data to negotiate with transit providers for guaranteed runs and routes connecting fringe parking or population centers to workplaces; design service schedules to match employee work patterns (routine eight-hour day vs. irregular hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply minimal charges at headquarters/similar problem locations; define who pays minimum fee
rubrics_metrics.description: '...support a recommendation that minimal charges be applied at Headquarters and buildings with similar problems.' / 'Those unable to use this service for legitimate reasons, and essentially this would mean only those in car pools or working unusual hours, would be subject to the minimum parking fee.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where alternatives are limited (e.g., headquarters buildings), set minimal parking charges rather than large fees. Define clear criteria for who is subject to any minimum fee (the memo suggests those unable to use provided transit services, with particular attention to carpoolers and irregular-hour workers) and document legitimate reasons for exemption.
